name: Cryptopanic bearish-vote spike as panic-velocity trigger (long)
rationale: MECHANISM: velocity variant that reads panic-in-progress from a DIRECT crowd tally — a surge in cryptopanic_bearish_votes crossing UP through a fitted spike level marks fresh, active retail pessimism (forced sellers voting with their fear), distinct from the slow-moving composite fear_greed. When that vote spike coincides with a same-day price drop (ret_Nd), it is a flush, and patient capital absorbs it. Long the snapback; exit when the vote pressure subsides (bearish votes cross back down) or stop/TP/time. Distinct from the fear_greed-velocity spec because the raw vote count is granular and NOT constructed from price, so it is a cleaner orthogonality test. DISCONFIRMER: check per-symbol coverage of cryptopanic votes FIRST — thin data collapses effective-N and the Gate rightly kills it. If bearish-vote spikes predict returns EQUALLY whether or not price also dropped, the price-confirmation adds nothing and it is a bare bearish-vote contrarian — test that simpler form instead.
catalyst: a fresh spike in bearish crowd votes into a price drop
